sentences.en: A Volcanoes are the ultimate earth-moving machinery.

sentences.en: A violent eruption can blow the top few kilometres off a mountain, scatter fine ash practically all over the globe and hurl rock fragments into the stratosphere to darken the skies a continent away.
sentences.zh: 暴发可能把山顶数公里外的顶部炸飞,几乎把精细的灰烬散布到全球各地,并将碎石碎片扔进平流层,使大陆以外的天空暗淡。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: But the classic eruption – cone-shaped mountain, big bang, mushroom cloud and surges of molten lava – is only a tiny part of a global story.
sentences.zh: 但经典的火山爆发 — — 锥形山、大爆炸、蘑菇云和熔岩的激增 — — 仅仅是全球故事的一小部分。

sentences.en: Volcanism, the name given to volcanic processes, really has shaped the world.
sentences.zh: 火山过程的命名火山现象确实塑造了世界

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Eruptions have rifted continents, raised mountain chains, constructed islands and shaped the topography of the earth.
sentences.zh: 火山爆发使大陆分裂,山链升高,岛屿建造,地球地形形成。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The entire ocean floor has a basement of volcanic basalt.
sentences.zh: 整个洋底都有一座火山岩层的地下室

sentences.en: Volcanoes have not only made the continents, they are also thought to have made the world’s first stable atmosphere and provided all the water for the oceans, rivers and ice-caps.
sentences.zh: 火山不仅造就了大陆,而且被认为是创造了世界上第一个稳定的大气层,为海洋、河流和冰盖提供了所有水。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: There are now about 600 active volcanoes.
sentences.zh: 现在约有600座活火山。

sentences.en: Every year they add two or three cubic kilometres of rock to the continents.
sentences.zh: 每年它们都会在大陆上增加两三立方公里的岩石。

sentences.en: Imagine a similar number of volcanoes smoking away for the last 3,500 million years.
sentences.zh: 想象一下过去35亿年中火山喷发的数量与火山喷发的数量相似

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: That is enough rock to explain the continental crust.
sentences.zh: 足够解释大陆地壳的岩石了

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: What comes out of volcanic craters is mostly gas.
sentences.zh: 火山坑中产生的主要是气体

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: More than 90% of this gas is water vapour from the deep earth: enough to explain, over 3,500 million years, the water in the oceans.
sentences.zh: 90%以上的气体是深土的水蒸气:足以解释超过35亿年的海洋水。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The rest of the gas is nitrogen, carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, methane, ammonia and hydrogen.
sentences.zh: 其余气体是氮、二氧化碳、二氧化硫、甲烷、氨和氢。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The quantity of these gases, again multiplied over 3,500 million years, is enough to explain the mass of the world’s atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 这些气体的数量再次乘以35亿年以上,足以解释世界大气的数量。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: We are alive because volcanoes provided the soil, air and water we need.
sentences.zh: 我们活着是因为火山提供了我们所需要的土壤、空气和水。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: If the shell is even slightly cracked during boiling, the white material bubbles out and sets like a tiny mountain chain over the crack – like an archipelogo of volcanic islands such as the Hawaiian Islands.

sentences.en: Sometimes it is slow: vast bubbles of magma – molten rock from the mantle – inch towards the surface, cooling slowly, to show through as granite extrusions (as on Skye, or the Great Whin Sill, the lava dyke squeezed out like toothpaste that carries part of Hadrian’s Wall in northern England).

sentences.en: In the Deccan plateau in western India, there are more than two million cubic kilometres of lava, some of it 2,400 metres thick, formed over 500,000 years of slurping eruption.

sentences.en: Sometimes the magma moves very swiftly indeed.

sentences.en: The biggest eruption are deep on the mid-ocean floor, where new lava is forcing the continents apart and widening the Atlantic by perhaps five centimetres a year.

sentences.en: During quiet periods, volcanoes cap themselves with their own lava by forming a powerful cone from the molten rocks slopping over the rim of the crater; later the lava cools slowly into a huge, hard, stable plug which blocks any further eruption until the pressure below becomes irresistible.
